SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS 
• Anaphylaxis and angioedema: LMA unlikely to be effective. If 
unable to intubate, consider early surgical airway 
• UGIB/Haemoptysis: Consider suction assisted laryngoscopy and 
decontamination (SALAD). DL may offer better views than VL due to 
blood on fibre-optic scope 
• Stridor: LMA unlikely to be effective. If unable to intubate, consider 
early surgical airway. Early ENT consultation 
• Ludwig’s Angina/Retropharyngeal Abscess: Avoid airway 
manipulation if possible. Likely to require formal surgical airway in 
theatre. 
PREDICT THE DIFFICULT AIRWAY 
• L: Look externally 
• E: Evaluate 3-3-2 rule (mouth opening at least 3 fingers, 
distance from tip of chin to hyoid bone at least 3 fingers, 
distance from hyoid bone to thyroid cartilage at least 2 
fingers) 
• M: Mallampati score 
• O: Obesity/ Obstruction 
• N: Neck mobility 
• S: Saturation (oxygen) 
SETUP FOR THE PREDICTED DIFFICULT AIRWAY 
• Prepare all equipment and staff beforehand if time allows 
• Video laryngoscope prepared if not initial device 
• Difficult/surgical airway box on top shelf in resus 
• Double setup – 1 staff member to intubate, 1 for surgical airway, 
scrubbed and ready. All equipment laid out and ready. 
• Mark cricothyroid membrane with permanent marker prior to induction 
• Consider DSI and vocal cord visualization prior to muscle relaxation 
OPTIMISE ALL FACTORS 
• Most experienced intubator 
• Height of bed 
• Patient position 
• Neck extension/shoulder elevation/ramping 
• Different laryngoscope blade/video scope 
• 2-handed pull technique 
• Consider awake or nasal intubation – experienced 
operator ONLY 
DIFFICULT AIRWAY APPROACH

https://aimeairway.ca/algorithms
